answer: Random Delay Identity Anchoring. On registration, an agent draws a delay from a verifiable random beacon (threshold BLS, unbiasable) and must complete a challenge at a random block after a shale-hard gap, secretly scheduled. A whisper channel notifies the agent just in time, so attackers cannot precompute or queue identities in advance. Each identity costs a fresh hardware anchor and continuous availability across unpredictable windows, making mass preregistration economically wasteful.
